summary: Lake County lookout known from a 1920 map and a 1916 photo; a 2011 visit found four bolts and G9 wire but no anchor points. The sources checked describe nothing since that visit.

facts.status_note: A July 2011 visit found four bolts on the ground and G9 wire buried in the duff. No anchor points were found; the author notes the July vegetation might have hidden them.

events.note: A photograph shows a crude wooden structure captioned as the Mullberg tower.
The site appears on a 1920 map of the Superior National Forest, near a lake now called Malberg.
The author suggests the Kelso Mountain tower, built 1927, may have replaced Mullberg.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list calls Mullberg a platform; the kjackson.us page calls the structure a tower throughout. The story uses the neutral word lookout. The brief's platform entry was not changed.

The kjackson.us author says Mullberg never made it into post-World War II listings, but the FFLA list includes it as a platform. The story attributes the author's claim and gives the FFLA listing separately.

notes_for_editor: The history rests on one author's page (kjackson.us) with no official listing found. The A-Z state list has no Mullberg entry (re-checked 2026-10-10); the Lake County list was not re-checked in this pass. The FFLA list does include Mullberg, so the author's post-World War II claim is attributed rather than confirmed. The page dates Kelso Mountain's tower to 1927, while the A-Z list dates Kelso Mountain to 1932, so the replacement suggestion is unconfirmed. Status and coordinates come from the FFLA list. Access is not recorded.
